prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct LongWordFinder and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: The point of Optional is that a caller never has to wonder whether null is coming back, so "returns null instead of Optional.empty()" is the bug that defeats the entire purpose of the return type -- and it only shows on an input where nothing matches. The word MORE in the contract is a strict comparison, so a word of exactly n letters is the boundary that separates > from >=. And FIRST needs a list with two matches in it: with only one match every implementation here agrees.
hints: You need an input where NOTHING matches. That is the only way to see an implementation that returns null rather than Optional.empty() -- and check for null before calling .isPresent(), or your own checker crashes.
MORE than n is strict: a word of exactly n letters must not be returned. ["abc"] with n = 3 is that boundary.
Put TWO long-enough words in one list so that returning the first and returning the last give different answers.
